name: gpt-anime-denoise
cost: Free (MIT code); models download under their own licenses
works_with: Claude Code, Codex; NVIDIA, AMD, Apple Silicon or CPU
short: Removes the fish-scale noise that GPT image models leave in anime and illustration images, without redrawing the picture.
what: gpt-anime-denoise cleans the fine fish-scale texture and broken shading that GPT image models leave in anime style images. The default method shrinks the image to 60%, scales it back up with ESRGAN and smooths it with an L0 filter. It has a command line tool and a local web app with brushes to protect parts of the image. As a skill, it tells your agent to run the clean-up on every GPT anime image before handing it over.
who: People who make anime or illustration images with GPT image models. The README is mostly in Chinese, with a short English summary, so expect to use a translator.
needs: PyTorch, spandrel, numpy, pillow and psutil (or the one-step installer)
About 100 MB for models, downloaded on first run

steps.title: Get the code and install dependencies
steps.text: Clone or download the repo. The one-step installer detects your graphics card, shows what it will download, asks first and installs into a `.venv` in the folder.

steps.title: Add it as a skill
steps.text: Put the whole folder in `.claude/skills/gpt-anime-denoise/`, or your Codex skills folder.

steps.title: Clean an image
steps.text: Output goes to an `image_denoise/` folder next to it.

steps.title: Compare methods
steps.text: This runs seven methods and makes a 4×2 comparison sheet.

steps.title: Fine tune in the browser
steps.text: The local web app opens at http://127.0.0.1:7865/.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `python denoise.py image.png --all` on a GPT anime image and compare the results at full size.

watch: Models download from their authors' sites on first run, with SHA-256 checks. They are not MIT: APISR is GPL-3.0 and Real-ESRGAN is BSD-3-Clause.
Images are processed only on your computer.
The example images are not covered by the MIT licence and are not for commercial use.
Without a GPU it works but is much slower: about 28 seconds per image in the README's CPU test.
